title: GPU CI credential rotation and image promotion runbook
body:
Summary

Purpose
This runbook describes how to (1) rotate the CI credentials used by GPU provisioning and image-promotion pipelines and (2) promote GPU runtime images (golden bundles) to production pools with verifiable checks and quick rollback. It includes Terraform patterns, CI job templates, verification checks, SLO gates and an oncall procedure for emergency credential revocation.

Why this matters
- Poorly sequenced credential rotation can leave inference pools unable to pull images, reducing capacity and failing deployments.
- Promotion from CI to staging to prod must be atomic and verifiable; a wrong image in a GPU pool can cause model regressions.
- Most image-promotion outages so far happened while key rotation overlapped cross-account image copies.

Scope
All CI pipelines that build GPU runtime images, the Terraform modules that provision tenant GPU hosts and warm pools, and Redwood Inference's image-signing/attestation services.

Owner and contacts
- Owner team: engineering (Infra Reliability)
- Oncall for rollout windows: infra-oncall@redwood.com
- Escalation: Diego Ramos (Lead - GPU Infra), Evan Liu (CI/CD)

Terminology
- Golden image: signed OCI bundle used on production inference nodes.
- Image promoter: CI job that signs, copies and tags artifacts into the production registry.
- Promotion window: the period when an image moves from staging to prod and cross-account copies may still be running.

Safety principles
1) Sign images with versioned keys (KMS alias + key-id); verification checks key version metadata.
2) Promote to in-region canaries before the full fleet.
3) Rotate credentials in two phases, preflight then swap, with automatic rollback on failure.
4) Use short-lived credentials for CI agents; keep long-term secrets only in HSM-backed KMS.
5) Follow the promotion safety matrix below.

Promotion safety matrix
| Signal | Threshold | Action | Rollback trigger |
|--------|-----------:|--------|-----------------|
| Canary 99th latency increase | +40% vs baseline | Halt promotion, mark image suspect, run perf trace | Auto-revert to previous tag in 15m if >2 buckets exceed threshold |
| Error rate (5xx) | >0.5% absolute | Move all traffic off canary nodes, abort promotion | Full fleet rollback if persisted for 10m |
| Tokenization mismatch | any runtime error | Halt; capture failing prompt, block image | Manual rollback after investigation |
| Image signature verification failures | any | Stop promotion, alert security, revoke CI key version | Block until signature chain validated |
| Pull auth errors across >=2 regions | >=5% pull failures | Pause promotion; force ephemeral credential refresh | If persists 10m, automated rollback and revoke ephemeral role |

Preflight checklist
1) CI builds the image and signs it via the signing service (key alias: kms/gpu-image-signer); metadata includes key-version and build-id.
2) CI runs an inference smoke harness against the staging warm pool (tag: staging-smoke) and checks latency and correctness.
3) Terraform plan for registry permissions and cross-account roles is reviewed through tfsec/gate (tf-modules/registry-crosscopy, tf-modules/ephemeral-ci-role, tf-modules/warm-pool-provisioner).
4) Record promotion intent in the promotion ledger (tagged commit + promotion ticket).

CI pipeline example
- name: build-and-sign-gpu-image
  runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
  steps:
    - checkout
    - run: |
        docker build -t staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} -f infra/Dockerfile .
        docker push staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
    - uses: redwood/sign-image-action@v1
      with:
        image: staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}
        kms-key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/gpu/cryptoKeys/gpu-image-signer
    - run: |
        curl -X POST https://signing.redwood.internal/attest -d '{"image":"staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}}","key_version":"v2"}'

Promotion job (partial)
- name: promote-to-canary
  env:
    EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
  steps:
    - assume-role $EPHEMERAL_ROLE_ARN --duration 900
    - run: |
        ./scripts/cross-account-copy --src staging-gpu:${{GIT_SHA}} --dst prod-gpu:${{PROMOTION_TAG}} --regions us-west-2,eu-west-1
    - run: |
        terraform -chdir=infra/promotion apply -auto-approve -var='image_tag=${PROMOTION_TAG}'

Terraform patterns
- registry-crosscopy: models cross-account ECR/GCR copy permissions and a short-lived promotion task. Inputs: src_repo, dst_repo, allowed_regions, promotion_role_arn. Outputs: promotion_task_id, crosscopy_logs_s3.
- ephemeral-ci-role: IAM role assumed by CI for promotion; short sessions only, MFA for manual triggers, OPA policy against broad permissions.
- Remote state gating: promotion applies take a remote state lock plus a semaphore key in the central tfstate bucket so promotions never run concurrently.

Credential rotation protocol (two-phase)
Phase A: Preflight
1) Create a new KMS key version, key-vN.
2) Run sign-image-action against key-vN behind a feature flag for test signings that do not touch the promotion ledger; confirm attestation accepts key-vN.
3) Run a shadow cross-account copy with the ephemeral role and new signing metadata in all target regions.
4) Watch for pull auth regressions for 24h (or 3 release windows).

Phase B: Cutover
1) Schedule a change window (blind window under 30m).
2) Atomically point alias kms/gpu-image-signer at key-vN.
3) Revoke short-lived CI credentials tied to key-v(N-1) after 30m grace and rotate ephemeral role sessions.
4) Promote a canary image signed with key-vN. Verify canary health for 10m on latency and error metrics.
5) If nothing fires, promote to the full fleet; otherwise point the alias back to key-v(N-1) and mark key-vN revocation-pending for review.

Emergency rollback runbook (oncall)
1) Detect: pages for pull auth failures or mass CrashLoopBackOff on prod image pulls.
2) First 5 minutes:
   - Check cross-region registry metrics for pull auth error percentage.
   - If pull auth failures >=5% across >=2 regions, run ./scripts/revoke-ci-ephemeral-sessions --role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-ephemeral-publisher
   - On signature mismatch, block the image tag in the promotion ledger.
3) If still failing after 10m:
   - Revert affected warm pools to the previous production tag with terraform apply -var='image_tag=${PREV_TAG}'
   - Trigger the warm-pool rolling-replace job if nodes are stuck.
4) Afterwards: open an incident review with ledger entries, CI logs, KMS audit trail and session token logs.

Observability and SLOs
- Canary latency delta: canary 99th within +25% of baseline during the canary window.
- Image pull success: >=99.5% within 1m at steady state.
- Promotion lead time: preflight finishes within 90 minutes for standard releases; emergencies use the expedited path with a manual approver.

Dashboards
- Registry pull success by region and account (1m/5m)
- Signature verification failures by key-version
- Promotion job success/failure by commit
- Canary latency and error trends vs baseline, annotated with promotions

Required CI gates
- Attestation must validate signatures including key-version; mismatches fail the job.
- OPA admission check asserts a unique promotion_task_id and no concurrent promotion.
- Pre-promotion smoke harness: 100 inference prompts compared with a golden-response set (95% similarity threshold).

FAQ
Q: A region's image copy lags by more than 30 minutes?
A: Pause and re-run the crosscopy manually. If it still has not copied within 60 minutes, postpone full promotion and promote region by region.

Q: Who can trigger expedited promotions?
A: CI admins with MFA plus signed approval from the Release Lead and Security.

Appendix A - Ephemeral role Terraform stub
resource "aws_iam_role" "ci_ephemeral_publisher" {
  name               = "ci-ephemeral-publisher-${var.env}"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume.json
  tags = { team = "gpu-infra", created_by = "ci-pipeline" }
}

package promotion.gate

default allow = false

allow {
  not input.concurrent_promotion
}
